title: v0.27.1: multi-node accelerate launch + end-to-end validation
body:
## Context

v0.27.0 `build_accelerate_argv(num_processes, script_args, mixed_precision, num_machines)` does accept `num_machines > 1` and emits `--num_machines N` in the argv, but the multi-node path is not tested end-to-end:
- no `--machine_rank`, `--main_process_ip`, `--main_process_port` pass-through
- no rendezvous backend selection
- no test case that exercises a 2-node setup

## Proposal for v0.27.1

1. Extend `build_accelerate_argv` with optional `machine_rank: int`, `main_process_ip: str`, `main_process_port: int`
2. Add `--nodes N --node-rank K --master-addr X --master-port Y` flags to `soup train` that map through
3. Test a 2-machine launch via mocked `subprocess` + assert both nodes receive matching NCCL env + argv

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `soup train --gpus 8 --nodes 2 --node-rank 0 --master-addr head.internal --master-port 29500` prints a valid `accelerate launch` command for a 16-GPU 2-node setup
- [ ] NCCL `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0` suggestion when `num_machines > 1` (InfiniBand is typically the inter-node transport)
- [ ] Clear error message when `master-addr` is missing but `nodes > 1`
- [ ] New test class `TestMultiNodeLauncher` in `test_multi_gpu.py`

## Risk notes

- Multi-node testing requires either real hardware or a mocked `subprocess` + env-var assertions
- Firewall / port rules are the user's responsibility; doc it

comments.body:
I'll take this one. I checked the thread and open PRs and found no existing claim or overlapping multi-node PR.

The gap is still present on `main` at `e0fd219`: `build_accelerate_argv` accepts `num_machines`, but not the node rank or coordinator address/port, and `soup train` has no corresponding CLI options.

My scope:

- Add `--nodes`, `--node-rank`, `--master-addr`, and `--master-port`, with validation and forwarding into the Accelerate launch arguments.
- Cover the issue's two-node example, including total process count, matching coordinator settings, and distinct node ranks.
- Keep the printed launch advice consistent with auto-reexec, and preserve the dry-run and single-node behavior.
- Add `TestMultiNodeLauncher`, the requested NCCL advisory, and documentation of network prerequisites.

I'll use the CPU tests with mocked launch/environment checks allowed by the issue. I don't have a multi-node GPU cluster available for this contribution, so I won't claim a real distributed training run as validation.

@tristangrech — yours. One scoping note so the PR does not end up claiming something it cannot show.

This issue has two halves with very different verifiability:

**Verifiable without hardware, and this is the bulk of it.** `build_accelerate_argv` gaining `machine_rank` / `main_process_ip` / `main_process_port`, the `--nodes / --node-rank / --master-addr / --master-port` flags mapping through, the missing-`master-addr` error, the `NCCL_IB_DISABLE` suggestion, and `TestMultiNodeLauncher` asserting the argv and env a 2-node launch would produce. The acceptance criteria were written for a mocked `subprocess` on purpose. Land this half and the issue has earned its keep.

**Not verifiable without two machines.** The "end-to-end validation" in the title. Please do not mark that box unless you actually ran it, and if you do run it, say on what — two nodes over IB and two cloud VMs over TCP are different claims.

Two things I would ask for in the tests, both from scars this repo already has:

- Assert the **exact argv list**, not a substring of a joined string. A flag that lands in the wrong position still appears in the joined text.
- Any assertion on CLI output must strip ANSI and collapse whitespace before matching. Rich emits escapes *inside* flag names on colour-capable runners, so `"--node-rank" in output` fails on Linux and macOS CI while passing on Windows, where Rich auto-disables colour. This has turned CI red here four times; `tests/test_auto_tuning.py` has the canonical helper.

And the control that makes the mocked half worth anything: a test that fails if `machine_rank` is dropped from the argv. A mock-based launcher test that passes against a launcher which builds nothing is the default outcome, not a hypothetical one.

You have #655 open as well — no objection to holding both, just flagging it so you can sequence them rather than discover the overlap later.

Shipped in #853, thanks to @tristangrech.

Try:

```bash
soup train --config soup.yaml --gpus 8 --nodes 2 --node-rank 0 --master-addr head.internal --master-port 29500
```

Run the same command on every machine with its own `--node-rank`.

All four acceptance criteria are met on `main`:

- [x] `--gpus 8 --nodes 2 --node-rank K --master-addr X --master-port Y` prints a valid 2-node, 16-GPU `accelerate launch` command. `build_accelerate_argv` takes `machine_rank`, `main_process_ip` and `main_process_port` and emits `--machine_rank / --main_process_ip / --main_process_port / --rdzv_backend static`; `TestMultiNodeLauncher::test_exact_argv_for_each_node` pins the exact argv for rank 0 and rank 1.
- [x] `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0` when `num_machines > 1` — `utils/topology.py:suggest_nccl_env` keeps InfiniBand enabled across nodes and disables probing only for a local multi-GPU box.
- [x] Clear error when `--master-addr` is missing but `--nodes > 1`, plus the same for the other required combinations, parametrized in `test_multi_gpu.py`. `--master-addr` is also validated as an address rather than merely as a non-dash string, so a shell fragment or a URL is refused at parse time.
- [x] `TestMultiNodeLauncher` exists in `tests/test_multi_gpu.py`, CPU-only, no distributed training run.

Documented in `docs/commands.md` and `docs/performance-and-quantization.md`. Firewall and port rules remain the operator's responsibility, as the issue notes.

Two commits on that branch are mine, pushed on an announced date after the review items went unanswered: the `--master-addr` validation and the removal of the README front-door paragraph. The feature commit is @tristangrech's and is untouched; the split is stated on the PR.
